title: The app's own window order follows every window it orders front, also one ordered front without becoming key (cx-8w027.25)
preconditions: tagged bench build (no activation: a window ordered front does not become key)
a fresh launch: one window, one workspace, one terminal tab
converted from scripts/cmux-next/window-order-e2e.py, which stays; tests/oracle/corpus/e2e/_scripts-097.json links them

steps.note: the scenario of scripts/cmux-next/window-order-e2e.py (kept): three windows, then Select Previous and Select Next Window, each read from the windows facet's order (the window registry's recency, front first)
script check 'three new windows': each new window is ordered front, so the order is newest first

script check 'selectPreviousWindow raised <back window>': under no-activate WindowActivation orders the back window front without making it key, and WindowManager.windowDidOrder moves it to the front of the order; on 09711a45a4b (the parent of bc106793c4a) the order followed key-window changes only, so it did not change and this wait times out

invariants: at three-windows the windows facet lists 3 visible windows and its order names each of them once (where a new window goes under no-activate is WindowActivation's present rule; the baseline records it)
at previous-raised the order's first window is three-windows' last, and the other two keep their relative order
at next-raised the order's first window is previous-raised's second (Select Next Window cycles on from the front window, as the script expects), and the order still names each of the 3 windows once
the key window does not change in select-previous or select-next (no activation: the bench launch never makes the app active)
every mutation has one receipt or one typed error (I1)
ids stay stable unless the step created or closed them (I2)
teardown: quit the tagged app the run started
verify its debug socket is gone
untested: the script's cross-check against the window server's stacking (debug.windows z_order, NSApp.orderedWindows): a debug read no facet records; the case checks the app's own order record, which is what the fix keeps
the relaunch restack (the three windows come back in the same order): the app driver has no restart step yet (p15-oracle-023, p15-oracle-188)
